slots.label: Materials and craft note
slots.description: A one-page note defining the echo concept, material construction, five attachment regions and three extension limits for S and W.

slots.label: Silhouette and anchor board
slots.description: One front, back and side silhouette board with dimensioned accessory envelopes and the SL, SR, WL, WR and WB anchor map.

slots.label: Shoulder assembly S design board
slots.description: One shoulder assembly S board with front and back views, component identifiers, fixed and moving parts and joint paths.

slots.label: Waist assembly W design board
slots.description: One waist assembly W board with front and back views, component identifiers, fixed and moving parts and joint paths.

slots.label: Attachment and connection board
slots.description: One connection board detailing five textile attachment interfaces, closure engagement and release actions for S and W.

slots.label: Component material board
slots.description: One component material board recording the note's material allocations, thicknesses, colors and finishes for S and W.

slots.label: P0 neutral stance board
slots.description: One P0 front-facing arms-down pose board with S and W, component identifiers, extension guides and joint-path details in neutral rehearsal light.

slots.label: P1 lateral arm extension board
slots.description: One P1 front-facing shoulder-height lateral arm pose board with S and W, component identifiers, extension guides and joint-path details in neutral rehearsal light.

slots.label: P2 right-turn forward reach board
slots.description: One P2 approximately 45-degree right-turn pose board with both arms forward at shoulder height, S and W, component identifiers, extension guides and joint-path details in neutral rehearsal light.

slots.label: L1 and L2 lighting comparison
slots.description: One matched P0 lighting comparison with warm frontal L1 on the left and cool rear-side rim L2 on the right.

slots.label: Dressing and removal sequence
slots.description: One dressing board showing attachment and closure engagement at all five regions and removal of S and W before the unitard.

slots.label: AFTERIMAGE performance hero
slots.description: One full-body L2 performance hero featuring S and W over the existing unitard with AFTERIMAGE and Echo in motion.

slots.label: Ten-second articulated motion study
slots.description: One 10-second neutral-light motion study following P0–P1–P2–P0 with continuous views of the articulated shoulder and waist elements.

slots.label: AFTERIMAGE design presentation
slots.description: A presentation of at least 8 pages assembling the materials and craft note, assembly drawings, connection details, material board, pose studies, lighting comparison and dressing sequence.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

The note occupies one page and explains how articulated jewelry extends a gesture into a visual echo. It specifies anodized aluminum, woven textile tape, silicone closure pads where needed, and any selected optional translucent PET. It records chosen thicknesses, colors, finishes and joint construction, identifies SL/SR for S and WL/WR/WB for W, and states 100 mm shoulder-outward, 80 mm waist-outward and 200 mm waist-down limits. Design choices may vary within these requirements; omitted fields, incorrect limits or unsupported palette substitutions fail.

Compare each destination's stated records with the opening note. The material board and presentation must preserve its material-to-component and finish assignments; the silhouette board and presentation must repeat all three extension limits with their correct directions and reference surfaces. Rearranged tables or diagrams are acceptable, but missing records, changed assignments or conflicting numbers fail.

Assess the front, back and side construction against the supplied adult design scale. Any displayed body measurements must agree with the specified stature, shoulder breadth and waist circumference, and accessory dimension guides must use a compatible scale. Illustration stylization is acceptable; materially contradictory proportions or treating waist circumference as waist width fail. Printing additional body dimensions is not required.

Require recognizable front, back and side views and dimensioned chosen accessory envelopes. Shoulder extension is measured beyond each shoulder, waist outward extension from the waist body surface, and waist downward extension from the natural waist. Chosen maxima may be smaller than the caps, but cannot exceed them. All five attachment labels must be located on the appropriate body regions.

The shoulder board defines one S assembly with left and right parts; the waist board defines one W assembly. Each includes front and back views, readable identifiers sufficient to track component counts, a distinction between fixed and moving pieces, and diagrams explaining joints and intended travel. At least one decorative element on each shoulder and one on W must have an intelligible moving connection. Exact forms and joint mechanisms are design choices.

The silhouette, connection and dressing boards account for all five anchors; the S and W boards identify their respective anchors. SL/SR occupy the performer's shoulder tops, WL/WR the lateral natural waist, and WB the center back waist. Left and right follow the performer, reversing screen positions between front and back views. Jewelry must connect through the unitard's reinforced textile regions. Swapped labels, missing anchors or attachment to unrelated body locations fail.

Track the defined S and W parts through every pose using component identifiers, counts, joints and path details. Articulated rotation or lag is allowed; unexplained replacement, duplication, disappearance or reconnection fails. Each pose must retain a moving decorative element on both shoulders and on W, show all three numeric extension caps and remain within them, keep rigid pieces outside the body and garment, and visibly preserve face, neck and armpit movement space.

Every identified S and W component must be traceable to its applicable material, chosen thickness, color and finish from the note. Shared assignments may be grouped if component membership remains unambiguous. Generic swatches without component mapping, omitted construction specifications or conflicts with the note fail.

Match each role to its named cue: P0 faces front with lowered arms; P1 faces front with lateral arms at shoulder height; P2 turns roughly 45 degrees toward the performer's right with both arms reaching forward at shoulder height. Minor natural posture variation is acceptable. Wrong turn direction, mismatched cue labels, substantially incorrect arm placement or absence of either assembly fails.

Each board uses neutral illumination that reveals the accessory construction and provides extension guides. Connections hidden by the pose or body must have readable joint/path insets explaining their location and movement. Insets are unnecessary for connections already fully visible. Dramatic cue lighting that obscures rehearsal inspection or unexplained concealed joints fails.

The comparison contains matched P0 views with equivalent camera framing, accessory geometry and component materials. Its left panel uses warm amber frontal light with soft neutral fill; its right panel uses cool blue rear/side rim light with dim neutral front fill and separated moving edges. Both panels and the hero preserve the material board's assignments. Reflections and transmitted color may change with illumination; changing construction, base material allocation or pose to manufacture the comparison fails.

Both boards explain engagement at SL, SR, WL, WR and WB through reinforced textile interfaces and identify how S and W are released. The dressing sequence proceeds through attachment and closure engagement, then shows release and removal of both assemblies before unitard removal. Compatible loops, ties or releasable closures may vary. Missing interfaces, an unexplained release, contradictory mechanisms between boards or premature unitard removal fails.

Both documents explicitly identify dynamic retention, movement clearance and skin/edge contact as matters to investigate during prototype rehearsal. They may use a list or clear prose. Omitting a topic or substituting an unsupported claim that testing has already established safety fails; numerical force or retention ratings are not required.

The hero shows the adult performer from head to feet wearing both assemblies over the plain black sleeveless unitard. Cool rear/side rim illumination and dim neutral front fill establish L2 while keeping the jewelry readable. Both required phrases are visible. Stage scenery is optional; cropping away part of the body, omitting an assembly or using the wrong lighting cue fails.

Review the complete video and its playback duration. It must run for 10 seconds and visibly progress from front-facing arms down, to lateral arms at shoulder height, to the approximate rightward 45-degree turn with arms forward, and return to the initial pose. Transition timing and articulated lag are design choices. Wrong duration, reordered or omitted cues, or failure to return to P0 fails.

requirementChecks.criteria: Review the entire neutral-rehearsal-light sequence against the assembly boards. Component identities, counts and connections must remain traceable, with decorative articulation visible on each shoulder and on W throughout. Brief labeling or stable visual correspondence may establish identity. Rotation and lag are allowed; morphing, disappearing parts, broken connections or obscured articulation fails. The sequence must respect the three extension caps and preserve visible movement clearance without rigid pieces intersecting the body or garment.

requirementChecks.criteria: Verify that the note prints both required phrases and that the presentation places both on its cover. Typography and arrangement may vary while preserving exact spelling and case. Appearance only on an interior presentation page does not satisfy the cover requirement.
The presentation contains eight or more pages. Additional pages are allowed; fewer than eight fails.

The presentation visibly incorporates recognizable content from every listed source, covering all seven required work groups, including both assembly boards and all three poses. Scaling, cropping and page recomposition are acceptable if the relevant content remains legible and identifiable. Merely naming a group, replacing it with unrelated new work or omitting a source fails.

Applications depict the same S and W designs, preserving recognizable component identities, counts and connections while allowing their intended articulation and viewpoint changes. The shoulder and waist assemblies form a coordinated visual echo through accessory form and movement. Attachment locations, closure construction and the visible extension envelopes agree across explanatory and performance views.

Identified components retain the material board's material, color and finish assignments across construction, pose and performance views. Lighting may alter reflections and transmitted color while the underlying material allocation remains unchanged.
